title: Specs Guidelines Sidecar Schema
description: What whoever uses a component must observe when arranging it, authored beside the spec as guidelines.yaml. The audience is a consumer, not a builder — what a builder must implement is supplemental.schema.json's subject. An entry is a guideline item as the Design System Documentation Specification (DSDS) 0.23.1 defines one; the document is not a DSDS document, since DSDS requires kind and for on every section and this carries neither, so an exporter wraps a concern's entries in a DSDS section. Three scopes share this shape, and entries across scopes are additive rather than overriding (DSPEC-56). (ADR-118)

useWhen.description: What each subject in a set is for.

dontUseWhen.description: Which subjects are off-limits, why, and what replaces them.

anatomy.description: Rules about the element tree: what parts a component has and how they nest.

props.description: Rules about the props a component takes, and what a caller may pass.

styles.description: Rules about the style values a component's parts carry.

slotComposition.description: Rules about what may fill a slot, in what quantity, and in what arrangement.

events.description: Rules about what a component emits, and when.

accessibility.description: Rules about what assistive technology receives, and what a caller must supply for it.

behavior.description: Rules about what a component does in response to interaction or state.

motion.description: Rules about how a component traverses a change rather than where it ends up.

layout.description: Rules about how a component's parts are arranged and sized relative to each other.

overrides.description: Rules about what a caller may replace or supply in place of a component's own part.

naming.description: Rules about why a component, prop, or part carries the name it does.

Section.description: Rules for one concern a consumer must observe.

ObligationLevel.description: How strongly a guideline binds, with RFC 2119 semantics. DSDS 0.23.1 defines the first four; may is RFC 2119's fifth and is added here, because a permission recorded as should asserts an obligation the system does not hold.

oneOf.description: An absolute requirement; a usage that disregards it is wrong. Often written instead as required, or always.
A strong recommendation; disregard it only with a considered reason. Often written instead as recommended, or prefer.
A strong recommendation against; do it only with a considered reason. Often written instead as avoid.
An absolute prohibition; a usage that does it is wrong. Often written instead as never.
A permission the system grants, and neither requires nor discourages. Often written instead as optional, or could.

GuidelineEntry.description: One rule a consumer must observe.

statement.description: The rule itself, as a sentence a reader can act on.

alternatives.description: What to use instead, when the remedy is a thing this can point at. Preferred over instead whenever the remedy can be named, because a pointer resolves and a sentence does not.

instead.description: What to do instead, when the remedy is a rule rather than a thing. An exporter folds this into statement rather than dropping it (DSPEC-59).

refines.description: A broader guideline this one elaborates.

checks.description: What does the checking. Required when checkedBy is automated.

SelectionSubject.description: One thing in a set, and what it is for. Exactly one of $token or $name is present. A token is identified by the path the rest of the system spells it with, spaces and capitals included — a DSDS-legal identifier is derived at export (DSPEC-60), never authored here.

$token.description: The token this is about, as a <collection>/<group>/<name> path.

$name.description: The prop, variant or slot fill this is about.

$description.description: What it is for, or why it is off-limits.

alternatives.description: What to reach for instead of this one. Meaningful under dontUseWhen, where its absence says something true: nothing replaces this subject.

refs.description: Related references, including same-as when this restates a subject at another scope.

SelectionGuidance.description: Subjects grouped by what kind of thing they are. A set of thirty tokens is a table a reader scans, not thirty rules a reader works through, which is why selection guidance is its own shape rather than one entry per subject.
